extra.message: User-controlled search text is concatenated directly into a SQL query string passed to db.all(). searchText originates from req.body.searchText in routes/search.js:11 (POST /search) and req.query.searchText in routes/api.js:7 (GET /api/search), and is interpolated into the SQL string at service/search.js:6 without parameterization (the parameterized version is commented out on line 7). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. a searchText of "' UNION SELECT id, username, password FROM user --" exfiltrates the plaintext usernames and passwords stored in the user table, or "%' OR 1=1 --" dumps every row.

Reflected cross-site scripting via unescaped template output. views/searchResult.pug line 4 uses the unescaped interpolation operator (h1!= 'Search Results for: ' + searchText), so the user-supplied searchText submitted through the POST /search form (routes/search.js:11, rendered via res.render('searchResult', ret) at routes/search.js:17) is emitted as raw HTML. A payload such as executes in the victim's browser, enabling session/cookie theft and other script-driven attacks.

extra.message: The error page renders the full error stack trace to remote clients. views/error.pug line 6 outputs `pre #{error.stack}`, and the guard in app.js:42 only suppresses the error object when the environment is not 'development'. NODE_ENV is never set to production anywhere (not in bin/www, package.json, or the Dockerfile), so the Express default of 'development' is active in deployment and any 500 error (e.g. one triggered via the SQL injection in service/search.js) leaks internal stack traces, file system paths, and framework details to attackers.

extra.message: Raw internal error object returned to the client. When the database query fails, routes/api.js line 12 responds with res.json(err), serializing the sqlite3 error object (error codes, database error details, and message content) directly to the remote caller instead of a sanitized, generic error response. Combined with the SQL injection in service/search.js:6, malformed injected queries cause database error details to be disclosed to the attacker, aiding further exploitation.

extra.message: User-controlled input is written to application logs without sanitization. routes/api.js lines 8-9 log the entire req.query object and the searchText value verbatim via console.log. An attacker can submit a searchText containing newline characters or forged log entries, allowing log forging/corruption of the application's output logs, which undermines audit trails and log-based monitoring.
